en: The Therāpadāna:
The Section on the Givers of Fruit (Phaladāyakavagga) 1.
The Apadāna of the Elder Kurañciyaphaladāyaka (The Giver of Kurañciya Fruit)
“In the past, I was a deer-hunter,
wandering through the forest;
there I saw the stainless Buddha.”
To the one who has gone beyond all phenomena,
I took a kurañciya fruit and gave it to the Best of Buddhas.
With my own hands, full of faith, I made offerings to that Tathāgata, a field of merit;
thirty-one eons ago from now...
Whatever fruit I gave back then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that gift of fruit.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
like an elephant that has severed its tether, I am free.
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has been mine in the presence of the Best of Buddhas.
The three true knowledges have been attained;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical insights—
And these eight liberations have been realized; the six direct knowledges have been attained;
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.”
Thus indeed the venerable elder Kurañciyaphaladāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Kurañciyaphaladāyaka.
